claim: Scouting pass, no theorem activated. The signed Fibonacci (no-lone) laws fail on many small cubic systems (census of all 60 connected cubic bipartite graphs with 2n <= 16, irregular counts, failures global) and are NP-complete to decide on cubic systems: a five-line gadget forces a port to a constant, a no-lone line with a constant point is an equality, so chains of copies give unbounded fan-out and Schaefer's theorem applies (reduction checked on 60 instances). Not-all-equal gadgets with up to 5 internal points reach only three relations (nothing, everything, itself); Fibonacci gadgets reach fifteen, including constants. Interest 1/3 (the hardness), 2/3 (rigidity of not-all-equal gadgets at all sizes).
conclusion: The Fibonacci knot has no mutual selection; together with lanes A and B, mutual selection is special to the knot among symmetric three-place laws.
